newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan 'Big Bang' to boost GDP and jobs - MITI panel.
newsitem.headline: Japan 'Big Bang' to boost GDP and jobs - MITI panel.

text.p: The implementation of "Big Bang" financial reforms would add about 0.3 of a percentage point to Japan's annual GDP growth rate, an advisory panel to the Trade Minister said on Thursday.

The sweeping reforms, aimed at making Japanese financial markets globally competitive, could also result in annual job growth of 1.2 percent in Japan's financial industry, the MITI subcommittee for industrial finance said in a statement.

The panel estimated that the Big Bang would allow Japan's financial industry to achieve an annual growth rate of 4.9 percent and the total aggregate of services could expand to 36.5 trillion yen by 2005, compared with 24.0 trillion yen in 1995.
If the reforms are not implemented, the financial industry in turn could see negative annual growth of 0.5 percent and the aggregate of services may shrink to 22.6 trillion by 2005, the panel said.
"It can be estimated that the Big Bang financial reforms would boost gross domestic product growth by about 0.3 percentage point," the panel said.
The Big Bang would also boost financial service jobs to 2.31 million by 2005 from 2.09 million in 1994. Without reforms, jobs would decrease to 1.84 million by 2005, it said.
The panel also said that abolition of the securities transaction tax would result in a net increase in tax revenues.

The panel estimated that 372.6 billion yen in tax revenues would be lost if the transaction tax were to be scrapped. However, lower transaction costs, increase in transactions and subsequent rises in stock prices would boost revenues from capital gains and corporate taxes by 392 billion yen, it said.
Abolition of the tax, therefore, would result in a net tax revenue increase of about 19 billion yen, the panel said.
The group, made up of 19 members including academics, company directors and economists, plans to make its financial reform proposals by early June, a MITI official said.
